metadata.note: Brightline, the privately built and operated intercity railroad in Florida -- the first new private intercity passenger railroad in the United States in over a century. Service opened January 13 2018 between Fort Lauderdale and West Palm Beach, reached MiamiCentral on May 19 2018, and was extended to Orlando International Airport on September 22 2023, giving a 235-mile Miami-Orlando route. South of Cocoa it runs over the Florida East Coast Railway main, the same corridor drawn historically in florida_east_coast_railway.geojson, which had carried no scheduled passenger train since July 31 1968; north-west of Cocoa it runs on its own new line beside SR 528. SPLIT PER RULE 4: three features, because the operating name changed twice and the route changed once. Brightline 2018-2019 and 2020-2023 and Virgin Trains USA 2019-2020 all draw the original Miami-West Palm Beach line; the full Miami-Orlando route is a separate feature from 2023. Boundary years appear in two features, which is the same convention used elsewhere in this repo for ownership splits.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass API (maps.mail.ru mirror), bbox 25.70,-81.45,28.65,-80.00, ways filtered to operator/name matching Florida East Coast Railway, Brightline, All Aboard Florida or Virgin, with usage=industrial spurs excluded. Corridor-weighted Dijkstra over a 25 m node-merged graph between MiamiCentral and the Orlando International Airport station, corridor defined by the six Brightline stations plus intermediate FEC waypoints.

Station coordinates from OSM railway=station nodes tagged operator=Brightline: MiamiCentral 25.777652/-80.195724, Aventura 25.958443/-80.147264, Fort Lauderdale 26.123843/-80.145623, Boca Raton 26.353838/-80.087481, West Palm Beach 26.712015/-80.055359, Orlando International 28.411716/-81.307757.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Every headway_min is an estimate -- no Brightline timetable was consulted and the daily round-trip counts for each era were not checked. The Virgin Trains USA era is drawn as 2019-2020, but the rebrand was announced November 2018, was contractually due to complete by December 2019, and was never actually finished before the March 2020 shutdown, so the exact year at which the operating name changed is genuinely unclear and 2019 is a judgement call. Whether any Brightline trains ran under Virgin livery is not established here. Station stop patterns per era (which trains called at which stations) are not modelled.

properties.speed_source: Derived from published end-to-end journey times over the traced mileage, including stops. Brightline's posted maximum speeds are 125 mph Orlando-Cocoa, 110 mph Cocoa-West Palm Beach and 79-80 mph West Palm Beach-Miami; the figure here is an average, not a maximum.
properties.geometry_quality: Fully real-traced from OpenStreetMap -- the MiamiCentral to West Palm Beach half of the route traced for the Miami-Orlando feature in this file, cut at the West Palm Beach station (index 52 of 253, 0.34 km from the platform). 66.8 miles against Brightline's published 67 for the original South Florida service. All FEC main-line track; no straight-line approximation and no bridged gap over 60 m. See the Miami-Orlando feature's geometry_quality for the full method. Straight-line repair 2026-08-29: 1 ruled segment totalling 16 mi replaced with OpenStreetMap-traced rail geometry (see geometry_repairs for the OSM lines each one followed).

segments.note: Brightline opened January 13 2018 between Fort Lauderdale and West Palm Beach and extended south to MiamiCentral on May 19 2018 -- the first privately built and operated intercity passenger railroad in the United States in a century, running over Florida East Coast Railway track that had carried no scheduled passengers since 1968. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates from published journey times and rough service levels, not read off a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: the January 13 2018 opening and the May 19 2018 Miami extension are from the Brightline article; headway and speed are estimates.

segments.note: Brightline dropped the Virgin Trains USA rebrand and reverted to its own name in August 2020. Service had been suspended on March 25 2020 for COVID-19 and did not resume until November 8 2021, West Palm Beach to Miami -- every calendar year drawn here still carried some service (2020 to March 25, 2021 from November 8), so no year is drawn that had none, but roughly twenty months inside this segment had no trains at all. Boca Raton station opened December 21 2022 and Aventura December 24 2022. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates from published journey times and rough service levels, not read off a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: the August 2020 reversion to the Brightline name, the March 25 2020 suspension, the November 8 2021 resumption and the December 2022 Boca Raton and Aventura station openings are from the Brightline article and contemporary reporting; headway and speed are estimates.

segments.note: Brightline announced a partnership with the Virgin Group in November 2018 and renamed itself Virgin Trains USA, with the rebrand to be completed by December 2019; Richard Branson rebranded the Miami station in April 2019. CAVEAT WORTH KNOWING: the changeover was never finished and branding was inconsistent right up to the March 2020 shutdown, so treating 2019-2020 as a clean 'Virgin Trains USA era' -- which is what drawing it in its own colour does -- is a simplification. The affiliation was ended in August 2020 and the name reverted to Brightline. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates from published journey times and rough service levels, not read off a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: the November 2018 Virgin partnership and renaming, the December 2019 rebrand deadline, the April 2019 Miami station rebranding, the incomplete and inconsistent branding, and the August 2020 termination are from the Brightline press release and contemporary reporting; headway and speed are estimates.

properties.geometry_quality: Fully real-traced from OpenStreetMap -- no straight-line approximation and no bridged gap over 60 m anywhere on the route. 281.3 km follows ways named and operated 'Florida East Coast Railway', 60.6 km follows ways named 'Brightline - Orlando' operated by Brightline Trains Florida LLC (the purpose-built Cocoa-Orlando extension along SR 528), and 15.8 km is unnamed FEC- and Brightline-operated track at the terminals. Traced 234.4 miles against Brightline's published 235. All six stations fall within 250 m of the trace (MiamiCentral 0.02 km, Aventura 0.02, Fort Lauderdale 0.14, Boca Raton 0.01, West Palm Beach 0.04, Orlando International 0.05; the Cocoa junction where the route leaves the FEC is 0.23). Corridor-weighted Dijkstra over a 25 m node-merged graph, 2,626-point raw path Douglas-Peucker simplified at 20 m to 253 points. No reversals over 120 degrees and no revisits. This is current track, which for a service that began in 2018 is the correct alignment for every drawn year. Straight-line repair 2026-08-29: 2 ruled segments totalling 29 mi replaced with OpenStreetMap-traced rail geometry (see geometry_repairs for the OSM lines each one followed).

segments.note: The Orlando extension opened September 22 2023, taking Brightline 235 miles from MiamiCentral to the Intermodal Terminal at Orlando International Airport via Aventura, Fort Lauderdale, Boca Raton and West Palm Beach. North of West Palm Beach the route runs on Florida East Coast Railway track as far as Cocoa, then turns west onto 35 miles of Brightline-owned line built alongside SR 528. Maximum speeds are 125 mph Orlando-Cocoa, 110 mph Cocoa-West Palm Beach and 79-80 mph in the densely developed South Florida stretch. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates from published journey times and rough service levels, not read off a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: the September 22 2023 Orlando opening, the 235-mile route, the station list, the FEC/Brightline track ownership split at Cocoa and the three maximum-speed figures are from the Brightline article; headway is an estimate of an approximately hourly service and the average speed is derived from published journey time.
